user_reported_bug: The evidence-upload test test_nextgen_wave2a::test_upload_rgb_returns_hash_and_key fails because a previous run left the same SHA-256 record in a shared development database. Fix without weakening production duplicate-evidence protection.
summary: No relevant testing skill found. Commit 7586995 changes only backend/tests/test_nextgen_wave2a.py, with no /app/backend/nextgen production duplicate-detection changes.
critical_code_review_comments: git show for commit 7586995 lists only backend/tests/test_nextgen_wave2a.py; /app/backend/nextgen was untouched, so production duplicate-evidence protection was not changed by this fix.
The test helper now derives salt_bytes from hashlib.sha256(f'{_TEST_SUFFIX}:{seed}'.encode()).digest() and paints the salt into the PNG top row; same-run deterministic bytes are preserved.
seed_data_creation: Pytest runs created isolated Wave 2A test properties, missions, evidence rows, and local nextgen_storage artifacts using unique TEST_W2A suffixes; no manual seed data was created.

rca_of_the_issue: The previous test payload salting strategy allowed repeated SHA-256 content across runs in a shared dev database. The current fix makes the synthetic PNG payload unique per full millisecond suffix by deriving a 32-byte SHA-256 salt from the full _TEST_SUFFIX plus seed while keeping duplicate calls within the same run byte-identical for duplicate-detection assertions.
